edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production based on information reasonably available after a diligent inquiry. These responses state Defendant's objections with specificity and, where Defendant agrees to produce documents, identify the scope of the search and production. No responsive, non-privileged documents are being withheld on the basis of any general or preliminary objection unless expressly stated in a request-specific response or in these amended responses. Defendant preserves all applicable privileges, protections, and immunities, including the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, common-interest doctrine, and applicable privacy or confidentiality protections.

1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant objects to the Requests only to the following extent, and these objections apply only where expressly incorporated into a request-specific response: (a) to the extent a Request seeks documents protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, common-interest doctrine, or any other applicable privilege or protection; (b) to the extent a Request seeks documents not relevant to any party's claim or defense or not proportional to the needs of the case; (c) to the extent a Request is overbroad, unduly burdensome, vague, ambiguous, or duplicative; (d) to the extent a Request seeks documents outside Defendant's possession, custody, or control; and (e) to the extent a Request seeks confidential, proprietary, private, or commercially sensitive information before entry of an appropriate protective order or confidentiality agreement. Defendant will not withhold responsive, non-privileged documents solely on the basis of these General Objections unless the applicable request-specific response so states and identifies the category of documents withheld. Defendant's production of documents is not an admission that the requested materials are relevant, admissible, or within the proper scope of discovery.

2. PRODUCTION AND ESI PARAMETERS. Subject to the specific objections stated in response to particular Requests, Defendant will conduct a reasonable search for and produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control. Defendant proposes the following ESI parameters, subject to further meet-and-confer and entry of an appropriate protective order: (a) custodians: the Executive's direct supervisor, Human Resources lead responsible for the Executive's employment/separation, the in-house legal custodian most directly involved in the separation, and one finance/payroll custodian responsible for compensation or severance calculations; (b) date range: January 1 of the calendar year preceding the events alleged in the Complaint through the date of filing of the Complaint, unless a particular Request reasonably requires a different period; (c) sources: active email, reasonably accessible electronic files, HR/personnel records, payroll/compensation records, and relevant contract or policy repositories; (d) search terms: Defendant will propose search terms within five business days and will meet and confer in good faith regarding Plaintiff's proposed additions or modifications; and (e) excluded sources absent a showing of good cause: disaster-recovery/backup systems not used in the ordinary course, deleted/slack space data, legacy systems that are not reasonably accessible, and duplicative copies. Defendant proposes to produce ESI as single-page TIFF images with load files, extracted text/OCR, standard metadata fields where reasonably available, and native files for spreadsheets and other files not reasonably usable in image format. Paper documents will be scanned and produced in reasonably usable form. Defendant will begin a rolling production within 21 days after agreement on search terms and entry of a protective order, and will substantially complete production within 45 days thereafter, subject to volume, privilege review, third-party confidentiality issues, and any further agreement of the parties or order of the Court. Defendant will identify in its request-specific responses any categories of responsive documents withheld on the basis of an objection.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent Defendant withholds responsive documents on the basis of privilege, work-product protection, or other protection from disclosure, Defendant will provide a privilege log in accordance with the applicable rules and any agreement of the parties or order of the Court. The log will identify, to the extent required and without revealing privileged or protected information, the document type, date, author, recipients, general subject matter, and privilege or protection asserted. The parties should meet and confer regarding categorical logging, redaction logging, and exclusion of post-complaint litigation communications from any logging requirement.

4. RESERVATION AND SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will amend or supplement these responses as required by the applicable rules, court order, or agreement of the parties. Defendant reserves all objections to the use, relevance, materiality, or admissibility of any documents produced in response to the Requests.

The document appears to be discovery response language with ESI parameters and privilege/protective order reservations. No hidden-content categories were provided or indicated for removal in this review package.

receiver.message_back: Counsel, we appreciate the revisions, but Plaintiff cannot agree to production being delayed until after both a protective order and search-term agreement; please begin producing readily available personnel, HR, payroll/severance, policy, and separation-related documents within 14 days, with any confidentiality designation under an interim attorneys’-eyes-only agreement pending entry of the protective order. We are available to confer this week on search terms, custodians, native/metadata fields, and logging, but reserve all rights as to any narrowed date range, excluded sources, or request-specific withholding not yet identified with particularity.
